We use the identity $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x. \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =-(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =-(\frac{1}{2}-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
